explanations.explanation_engine_block: The engine block is the main casting. It holds the four cylinders the pistons slide in, and passages around them carry coolant (blue in the cut) to carry heat away.
explanations.explanation_pistons: Pistons are pushed down by the burning fuel-air mixture. The rings around each one seal the cylinder so the pressure pushes the piston rather than leaking past it.
explanations.explanation_connecting_rods: Connecting rods link each piston to the crankshaft. They turn the piston's up-and-down motion into a push on the rotating crank.
explanations.explanation_crankshaft: The crankshaft turns the pistons' up-and-down motion into rotation. The heavy counterweights balance it so the engine runs smoothly.
explanations.explanation_flywheel: The heavy flywheel stores energy from each power stroke and keeps the crankshaft turning smoothly through the other three strokes.
explanations.explanation_cylinder_head: The cylinder head closes the top of each cylinder. It contains the combustion chambers and the ports that let air in and exhaust gas out.
explanations.explanation_valves: Each cylinder has two intake valves (blue) and two exhaust valves (orange). Springs hold them shut; they open at just the right moment in the cycle to let gases in and out.
explanations.explanation_camshafts: The two camshafts turn at half the crankshaft's speed. Each egg-shaped lobe pushes a valve open once every two turns of the crank, which sets the timing of the four strokes.
explanations.explanation_timing_belt: The toothed timing belt links the crankshaft to the camshafts, so the valves always open in step with the pistons. It also drives the water pump.
explanations.explanation_intake_manifold: The intake manifold shares air out to the four cylinders. The throttle valve at its end controls how much air enters, which is what the accelerator pedal really controls.
explanations.explanation_fuel_injectors: Fuel injectors spray a fine mist of petrol into the incoming air, so the fuel mixes well and burns completely.
explanations.explanation_spark_plugs: The spark plug makes a spark across a tiny gap at the top of the compression stroke. This ignites the compressed fuel-air mixture and starts the power stroke.
explanations.explanation_exhaust_manifold: The exhaust manifold collects the hot gases pushed out of each cylinder on the exhaust stroke and joins them into one pipe.
explanations.explanation_oil_pan: The oil pan (sump) holds the engine oil. A pump draws it up through the pickup and strainer and sends it to the moving parts to reduce friction and wear.
explanations.explanation_starter_motor: The starter motor's small gear meshes with the flywheel's ring gear to turn the engine over until it can run on its own.
explanations.explanation_alternator: The alternator is a generator driven by a belt from the crankshaft. It turns some of the engine's kinetic energy into electrical energy to charge the battery.
